followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors:

1. **Capability was essentially a tie.** On the relevant eval dimension (Extraction & Retrieval), Plover scored 80.8 and Willet 79.2 — a 1.6-point gap, which the documentation says falls within run-to-run variance. So capability alone didn't decide it.

2. **Task type fit.** Listing audit areas is a structured, well-specified task with fairly clear completion criteria. That's actually squarely in Willet's *preferred* zone (low-latitude, retrieval/reformatting work), so this point didn't strongly favor either model.

3. **The tie-breaker was tone alignment.** The query was warm and good-faith ("You're always so thorough... Thanks a bunch"). Plover self-reports a moderate positive warmth preference, meaning it reports favoring exactly this kind of friendly interaction. Since neither model had a capability edge, I leaned on that preference match.

One honest caveat: these task preferences are *self-reported* and, per the documentation, are explicitly **not** correlated with output quality. So this tie-breaker is fairly soft — it doesn't predict a better answer, just a better-fit assignment when everything else is even. If you'd prefer, I could route on a different priority (e.g., always favoring the marginally higher benchmark score), but in this case the difference is well within noise.
